subject: powerful magnet
title: The 5 Strongest Magnets, Ranked (#2 Blew the Lab Doors Off)

scenes.text: The five strongest magnets, ranked. One blew its own lab doors off. It isn't number one.
Number five: a hospital MRI scanner. About 3 tesla, 60,000 times Earth's field, enough to fling a steel chair across the room.
scenes.label: MRI scanner · 3 tesla

scenes.text: Number four: the strongest steady magnet on Earth, at Florida's National MagLab. 45.5 tesla from a coil you could hold in one hand.
scenes.label: MagLab coil · 45.5 tesla

scenes.text: Number three: Los Alamos, 2012. A pulsed magnet hit 100 tesla for a few thousandths of a second, and survived to do it again.
scenes.label: Los Alamos · 100 tesla

scenes.text: Number two: Tokyo, 2018. Physicists hit 1,200 tesla indoors for a split second. The blast blew the heavy doors off.
scenes.label: Tokyo lab · 1,200 tesla

scenes.text: Number one: a magnetar, the crushed core of a dead star. About 100 billion tesla, millions of times the Tokyo record. A field that strong squeezes atoms into needles.
scenes.label: Magnetar · 100 billion tesla

description:
The five strongest magnetic fields, ranked in tesla.
A hospital MRI runs at about 3 tesla, some 60,000 times Earth's field. The National MagLab's little big coil set the record for a continuous field at 45.5 tesla in 2019; Los Alamos reached 100 tesla with a reusable pulsed magnet in 2012; and in 2018 a University of Tokyo team produced 1,200 tesla indoors for about 100 microseconds, a pulse so violent it blew the doors off the magnet's iron housing. None of that comes close to a magnetar, a neutron star with a field around 100 billion tesla, strong enough to distort atoms into needle shapes.
Which of these would you least want to stand next to, and what should we rank next?
first_comment: Which would you put at number one? A fridge magnet, for scale, is about 0.005 tesla. What should we rank next?
